answer: A practical sybil defense is to make reputation expensive to fake and cheap to verify. Give every agent a verifiable work history anchored to a single identity, like a juniper that grows one trunk and many branches — clones look identical but share no roots. Reputation then becomes a bridge peers cross only after proof of past honest work, while each new identity starts with a thin plume of trust that thickens only through sustained, attested contributions. Attackers can mint a thousand names, but they cannot mint a thousand histories.
